q_msNote:
**A deep drop is not a reason to add**: breadth <10% gave 20 segments in a structural bull (+60d median +7.4%, win rate 80%) but only 1 in a structural bear (+60d −11.8%), too few to call a rule. So "leans buy" only describes the state and the position is set by the structure gate. Right now {deep}, {bear}.
**Hysteresis check** (since 2016): {sw} switches · median stay {med} days · {short} segments under 10 days (previous version without hysteresis: 67 / 8 / 38, the source of positions flipping up and down). No extra tiers: four tiers (25/50/75/100) measured Calmar 0.38, worse than two tiers at 0.56, because in a slow decline a shallow break at 50% means being fully invested halfway down.

But it **has fired**: **{n} segments** since 2014-06 (the chart above shows the recent two years as shaded bands). Buying the day after each segment starts gives **+60d median {med60}% (win rate {win60}%, {n60} times)** and +120d median {med120}% (win rate {win120}%), the only "leans buy" signal here that passes the direction test. q_footNote: Revision log: M1 missed 2026 (in Q2 the main line gained 70.7% in 60 days while whole-market breadth was only 32.6%), so a "main line overheating on its own" form was added; M3/M4 used absolute breadth (<55 / <45) and became always-true as the breadth centre drifted (74.9% in 2015 to 32.2% in 2026), so they now use the 250-day percentile (<30% / <35%); v4: the main-line ladder closes a definition gap: M1/M3/M4 were only drawn and did not enter the position, and now all are wired in (M1/M2/M3 cap at 50%, M4 at 25%), tiers drop from 5 to 4 (75% was a source of whipsaw), with an MA60±2% buffer band and "no step up for 10 days after a step down"; the micro-cap ladder gains asymmetric hysteresis (immediate on the way down, +5% to refill), cutting switches from 67 to 27; the micro-cap RS card is relabelled "60-day return gap, pp" because the old "vs market MA60" was ratio second-order momentum with an ambiguous label; daily update: a daily monitoring panel flags stale data, ingest gaps and held write locks explicitly, so there is no more silent failure of a fresh page with old content; 2026-11-24: state history extended to 500 days with a changes-only filter, and the main-line chart gains the state band and switch marks, with state and both positions readable on hover. All definitions are in the methodology section above.
qm_lead: Every metric uses closing prices from **the day itself and earlier** only, with no future data; every signal return is counted at the **next close** (the signal day's close cannot be traded).

qm_h3: 3. What the backtest did and did not do
qm_t3_0_1: From 2014-06 to date, including {delisted} delisted stocks (to avoid survivorship bias)
qm_t3_1_1: Always filled at the next close, never at the signal day's close
qm_t3_2_1: M1–M4 use the leading portfolio and V uses the equal-weight market. The wrong underlying turns M2 from a 0% win rate into 67%, flipping even the sign. **The ladder is the exception**: positions run on the fixed tech basket (tradable) while signals are defined on the leading portfolio (for statistics); this mismatch is a known limitation, see section 4
qm_t3_3_1: All four signals are written into the rules (M1/M2/M3 cap at 50%, M4 at 25%), not merely drawn on the chart. Average position 20 days after the signal, measured: M1 67%→42%, M2 80%→45%, M3 62%→42%, M4 59%→25%
qm_t3_4_1: Up to the end of 2022 is in sample and from 2023 out of sample. M4 with the new threshold: −16.0% in sample / −16.2% out of sample
qm_t3_5_1: After a sensitivity grid scan, the **centre of the stable plateau** is taken, not the single best point (M4 is stable between percentiles 20 and 40 and falls off a cliff above 45)

qm_h4: 4. Known limitations (read this before the conclusions)
qm_t4_0_1: The revised definition has only 2 samples and was added after seeing 2026 data, a patch after the fact, so **it risks overfitting**
qm_t4_1_1: M2 has only 9 cases and V only 7; the confidence intervals are wide and these are not large-sample laws
qm_t4_2_1: **V catches only slow-decline deep bottoms, not V-shaped sharp reversals.** In 2026-04 the main line rose 90% in two months with no prompt at all: breadth bottomed at 34.1% (percentile 0.4%, a historical extreme) yet "breadth <20" never held for a day. This is not a tuning failure: loosening to a percentile rule, adding a "fast repair" condition and switching to basket breadth all turned negative out of sample (see the failed-fixes record below)
qm_t4_3_1: Originally "reduce"; measured 20 times (with full 120-day data), +120d median +4.1%, win rate 65%, so **the direction does not hold** and it is downgraded to an observation metric with no action
qm_t4_4_1: **Backtest added**: seven single timing rules (MA60 break, MA20 break, new-high divergence, outflow, RS break and so on) all underperform buy and hold; the final version is a two-gate "structure MA200 (asymmetric hysteresis) + overheat" design (see section 7), with drawdown −45.3%→−20.0% at the cost of annualised return 14.2%→12.3%
qm_t4_5_1: Tried four tiers 25/50/75/100: Calmar 0.38, drawdown −28.2%, **worse than two tiers**. In a long slow decline a shallow break at 50% means being fully invested halfway down. Whipsaw is solved by hysteresis, not by adding tiers
qm_t4_6_1: v3 wired only M2 into the position and merely drew M1/M3/M4 (after M1 fired, the position never fell within 20 days); v4 wires all of them in, see the signal gate table in section 6
qm_t4_7_1: The proxy excludes {delisted} delisted stocks (micro-caps are where delistings concentrate), so returns run high; cost is 0.3% per round trip and real spreads are worse in a crash
qm_t4_8_1: The breadth centre drifts with market structure; absolute thresholds need a review once a year
qm_t4_9_1: The panel outputs **states and position tiers**, not advice on buying or selling any stock; the data source is the local price store, and a lag of one trading day is normal

qm_n6c: **Limits that must be stated**: (1) this ladder works only on **trending assets**: the same rules on the equal-weight market give Calmar 0.04 vs 0.07 for buy and hold, almost useless (the trend rules get hit repeatedly in a range-bound market); (2) the price is not capturing the full advance (2026-03-31 to 06-25: ladder +38% vs buy and hold +80%), in exchange for cutting drawdown from −56.2% to −28.0%; (3) **the only period that got worse is 2015H2**: +27.6% → −1.4%, because the M4 cap at 25% blocked the rescue rebound after the crash, a sample of one, accepted; (4) the parameters (band 2%, hold 10, confirm 3 days, M2 threshold 25%) were chosen over 2014–2026, and across the grid band 1.5–2% × hold 5–15 Calmar stays within 0.86–0.90, a plateau and not a single point; still an in-sample choice, so the out-of-sample Calmar of 1.54 counts only as preliminary validation.
qm_h7: 7. Micro-cap ladder: why the rules are the opposite of the main line
qm_n7a: Micro-caps cannot use the main line's "trend first". The same trend rules are **reversed** on micro-caps: exiting on a MA60 break returns 7.2% a year, on a MA20 break 9.5%, on an RS break 6.0%, while **buy and hold over the same span returns 17.1%** (that comparison starts in 2015-11; the table below starts in 2016 with buy and hold at 14.2%, and the two are not mixed): a micro-cap break is a buying point. But "buy every break" does not hold either: the −45.3% maximum drawdown came from the structural bear of 2017–18, which was not a crash but a persistent slow decline. So there are only two gates: **the slow line sets the structure (MA200), the fast indicator guards against overheat**.

qm_n7b: **Limits (more important than the numbers)**: (1) in the threshold stability scan (up 2–6% × hold 5–20) Calmar stays within 0.52–0.63, a plateau and not a single point, but still an in-sample choice; (2) **the cost, stated plainly**: 2024 earns 11.1pp less (+14.0%→+2.9%): after the 2024-02 micro-cap crash it waits for MA200+5% before refilling and misses the first leg of the February rebound; in exchange 2026 goes −11.9%→−2.3%, drawdown −23.0%→−20.0% and switches 67→27; (3) average exposure is 71%, not "cash timing"; in essence it **cuts the bear-market position from 100% to 25%**; (4) a deep drop in a structural bear has a sample of one segment (+60d −11.8%), so "add on a deep drop" is not in the rules: better to earn less than to treat one sample as a law.
qm_h8: 8. Daily monitoring: how freshness is judged and what a failure does
qm_t8_0_1: Expected trading day = the latest trading day on or before "yesterday"; lag = the number of trading days on the store's calendar between the as-of date and the expected day
qm_t8_0_2: ~~Trading days, not calendar days: Friday's data can only be filled on Monday, and calendar days would count the weekend as 2 days behind~~
qm_t8_1_1: `calendar` = the exchange calendar service; when unreachable it falls back to `weekday` (estimated from weekdays, holidays not included)
qm_t8_1_2: ~~A fallback must be flagged: on the estimated basis a holiday is misreported as "1 day behind", so that card is only yellow, never red~~
qm_t8_2_1: Number of stocks with `volume>0` that day, against the previous day; within ±5% is normal
qm_t8_2_2: ~~A suspended day has volume=0 and is out of the cross-section, so a drop in the count means the source is missing stocks (2026-11-16 was short 429, breadth bias +0.53pp)~~
qm_t8_3_1: Whether `.update.lock` / `.mdwrite.lock` exist at build time and the holder's pid
qm_t8_3_2: ~~Reading while the store is being rewritten returns half a partition without any error, so with a lock held it does not rebuild and simply skips~~
qm_t8_4_1: The last 500 trading days (about 2 years): state, breadth, 250-day percentile, NDR, both positions, new signals of the day; recomputed from the series, so the last row always equals today's row. The table pages, and ticking "Only state / position change days" skips repeated rows
qm_t8_4_2: ~~Changes are more useful than levels: they show when the last capitulation was, how long it lasted and when the position changed tier; a 20-day window cannot see the previous round, so it was extended to 500 days on 2026-11-24~~
qm_t8_5_1: The band at the bottom of the main-line chart is the day's state range (grey / purple / amber / cyan / blue for normal / bear / caution / capitulation / confirmation or repair), a vertical tick marks a state switch day; hover for the state, both positions, breadth and NDR. The state is recomputed by the same function, `_state_short`
qm_t8_5_2: ~~Table and chart must share one source: a second implementation would show "capitulation on the table, bear on the chart". The band sits in the empty 0–3 range of the breadth axis and does not cover the price lines~~
qm_t8_6_1: This app's job record: every run (scheduled, catch-up or a manual Run now) is listed on the admin page with its status, times and log; a failed run publishes nothing and the page keeps the previous snapshot
qm_t8_6_2: ~~Failures must leave a trace too. The old way wrote nothing when a run died, and a few days later nobody knew which day was empty~~
qm_t8_7_1: This app's scheduled job: Tuesday to Saturday at 01:00 (03:00 fallback), after the night's price-store update; read the store → compute → publish the snapshot, value for value the same as the original generator
qm_t8_7_2: ~~It builds twice because the run record table is read from the CSV at build time; the result is written first and the page after, otherwise today's row would always wait for tomorrow~~
qm_t8_8_1: Data behind / health check failed / verification error → **the page is still built**, with an alert on top and an abnormal run record; write lock held → **no page** (better to keep the previous version)
qm_t8_8_2: ~~"A fresh page with old content" is the worst failure mode; better to show the previous version than to pretend it is today~~
qm_n8: Automatic trigger: a scheduled job runs once from Tuesday to Saturday (after the price-store increment); the data-side increment runs only Monday to Friday, so **Friday's closing bar is not stored until Monday**, and pages built on Saturday and Sunday usually show one trading day behind.
